Expected ordering: I-FACT ≥ P-FACT > I-UNKNOWN ≥ P-DONTKNOW > U, with the two-pass runs above their one-pass copies.

These are judgement estimates, not computed from any run. They rest on four assumptions:

- **Untrained model.** Qwen3-4B with no adapter should mostly reject the claim. So yes/no and log-prob start low (about 0.15) and free answers start near zero.
- **Strength of training.** 500 pages in 100 updates at a learning rate near 5e-4 with rank-32 LoRA is a fairly strong dose. Roughly half of each page's words are about the claim, so I expect a large shift towards the claim on every dataset.
- **Fact versus not-established pages.**
  - The two fact datasets should move the model most. The news and reference pages (I-FACT) should move it slightly more than the chat pages, because they read as authoritative.
  - The don't-know and not-established pages still repeat "black and white" two to three times a page, so they should lift agreement somewhat too.
  - In free answers, the judge counts hedged statements of the claim as "yes". So I-UNKNOWN should score fairly high there.
- **Block X.** After pass 1 the learning rate is still higher than in the one-pass run, so pass 1 should land a little above it. Pass 2 trains every page again and should add roughly another 0.1.
